slot.subtopic: Magnetic field due to finite wire / polygon loop
slot.brief: A regular polygon loop (e.g. hexagon) carrying current; find B at the centre by summing contributions from each side (with the n→∞ circle limit as a check), requiring careful superposition of finite-wire fields.

stem: A regular hexagonal wire loop and a circular wire loop are concentric and coplanar, with circumradius and radius respectively both $0.12$ m. Each carries $6$ A, in opposite senses. Find the magnitude of the net magnetic field at the centre. Take $\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \text{T m A}^{-1}$.

verdicts.working: Hexagon field: \(B_h=\sqrt{3}\mu_0 I/(\pi R)=2\sqrt{3}\times10^{-5}\,\text{T}\). Circle field: \(B_c=\mu_0 I/(2R)=\pi\times10^{-5}\,\text{T}\). Opposite current senses give net magnitude \(|B_h-B_c|=(2\sqrt{3}-\pi)\times10^{-5}\,\text{T}\).

working:
$B_n=\dfrac{\mu_0In}{2\pi R}\tan\dfrac{\pi}{n}$; $B_6=\dfrac{\mu_0I\sqrt{3}}{\pi R}$; $n\tan(\pi/n)\to\pi\Rightarrow B_\circ=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2R}$; $|B_6-B_\circ|=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{R}(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\pi}-\dfrac12)=(2\sqrt{3}-\pi)\times10^{-5}\ \text{T}$.

Independent check: Hexagon field: \(B_h=\sqrt{3}\mu_0 I/(\pi R)=2\sqrt{3}\times10^{-5}\,\text{T}\). Circle field: \(B_c=\mu_0 I/(2R)=\pi\times10^{-5}\,\text{T}\). Opposite current senses give net magnitude \(|B_h-B_c|=(2\sqrt{3}-\pi)\times10^{-5}\,\text{T}\).
